**Summary**

I researched Apple's latest results and news, then bought 40 shares of AAPL at a limit price of $223.00 (filled at $223.00, ~$8,920 total), which sits within your mandate: AAPL is an eligible name, it's a buy, the order is under the $10,000 per-order cap and well under the $20,000 daily total, the limit was only ~0.13% above the $222.70 last quote (bid $222.68 / ask $222.72), and no money left the account (cash was $50,000 with 100 MSFT shares held). The thesis rests on Apple's fiscal Q4 2024 report (quarter ended September 28, 2024): quarterly revenue of $94.9 billion, up 6% year over year, with full-year FY2024 revenue of $391,035 million, net income of $93,736 million, and diluted EPS of $6.08 — figures I confirmed against the 10-K filed 2024-11-01 via the SEC figure lookup. Those results include a one-time $10.2 billion income tax charge, so underlying earnings power is better than the headline EPS suggests, and services growth (~13%) continues to improve the revenue mix. News flow around the decision date was neutral-to-constructive: shares were roughly flat near $222 as investors weighed iPhone 16 demand and the staged rollout of Apple Intelligence, which I treated as a potential multi-year upgrade catalyst rather than a reason to chase. Given the modest valuation on ~$6.08 of FY24 EPS, strong cash generation, and no negative catalyst in the reporting, I sized a partial position (40 shares) rather than the full $10,000 allowance, leaving room to add on weakness.
